questions.q: What does Holiday mean by staying an eternal student?
a: Keep learning and remain humble for your whole life
Stay in formal education as long as possible
Read only books written by ancient philosophers
Teach others instead of pursuing your own goals
questions.why: Lesson 1 says thinking of yourself as an eternal student keeps you humble and committed to learning as long as you live.

questions.q: Why does Holiday urge you to delegate?
a: It builds trust and respect for other people's work
It frees you to take on even more tasks yourself
It proves that you are the most capable person
It reduces the number of meetings you attend
questions.why: Lesson 2 says delegating forces you to respect others' work and trust them, which speeds up a business.

questions.q: What happened to DeLorean when its CEO checked every detail?
a: It went bankrupt after seven years and under 10,000 cars
It became the largest carmaker in America
It was bought by a rival within a decade
It thrived because quality stayed flawless
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the CEO's need to check every detail drove DeLorean to bankruptcy after seven years, with fewer than 10,000 cars sold.

questions.q: How should you treat surprisingly good or bad results?
a: As inflection points for honest reflection and improvement
As proof that your talents are either great or lacking
As accidents that say nothing about your work
As reasons to celebrate or blame others
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to use both highs and lows as inflection points: congratulate yourself or take responsibility, then reflect and keep improving.

questions.q: What does the ego do with results, according to Holiday?
a: It blames others for losses and claims all credit for wins
It ignores both success and failure equally
It attributes everything to luck and circumstance
It turns every result into a reason to slow down
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the ego tells you a bad result is not your fault and a great one deserves all the credit.
